notable_absence.finding: No role:/privilege: concept is cited: this command changes the CALLING user's own password, and the only authorization statement on the page is the shared generic 'unauthorized error' boilerplate that applies to every subcommand's -u/-p flags. Given that this is a self-service password change (any authenticated user changing their own credential, regardless of role), the absence of a role citation is arguably correct here rather than a gap - unlike the other pages in this batch, self-service password change is plausibly available to every role by design, so this is noted rather than pressed as a finding.

cross_component_finding: The SYNOPSIS line names the command `_couchbase-cli-user-change-password_` (hyphens joining 'couchbase-cli' to the subcommand name) instead of the two-word, space-separated form `couchbase-cli user-change-password` that every other subcommand page in this batch uses in its own SYNOPSIS (e.g. `_couchbase-cli master-password_`, `_couchbase-cli user-manage_`). This is a literal, mechanical inconsistency isolated to a single page - the kind of copy-paste slip (joining the tool name and subcommand name with a hyphen instead of a space) that a TW editing pass would normally catch, and a clean, minimal example of this round's authorship-provenance hypothesis about lighter review in cli/.
cross_product_finding: n/a - no Capella/Mobile/SDK content; self-service password change via couchbase-cli is a Server-only operation with no stated Capella CLI equivalent.
